key_insight: XANES and DFT+U indicate that oxygen vacancies in NdBaCo2O5+δ are distributed beyond the usual apical sites, helping explain the compound’s magnetic inhomogeneity and variable-range-hopping transport.
engineering_relevance: Controlling vacancy ordering in layered cobaltates could improve oxygen-ion mobility and enable faster, more sensitive oxygen-sensing materials.
method: Co K-edge, Ba LIII-edge, and Nd LIII-edge XANES analysis
DFT+U-based first-principles modeling of vacancy distribution
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that spectral features from the XANES data suggest δ is closer to 0.75 than the nominal ~0.65, and confirm Ba remains in the +2 oxidation state.
watch_item: The vacancy-site assignment is inferred from spectroscopy and modeling, so direct structural validation of the oxygen-vacancy distribution would strengthen the conclusion.
paper_title: X-ray absorption spectroscopic studies of oxygen-deficient double perovskite oxide NdBaCo$_2$O$_{5+δ}$ ($δ\sim 0.65$)
